subject: Advanced Database
title: MySQL, WAMP, PHP & Database Management - Comprehensive Quiz (60 Items)

questions.text: What does the acronym WAMP stand for?
questions.hint: It is a local development stack for Windows that includes a web server, database, and scripting language.

questions.text: When the WAMP tray icon turns green, what does it indicate?
questions.hint: Green is the healthy status for the WAMP icon.

questions.text: Where should you place your PHP files so they can be accessed via localhost?
questions.hint: This is the web root directory of WAMP.

questions.text: Which SQL sub-language is responsible for defining and modifying database structure (CREATE, ALTER, DROP)?
questions.hint: It stands for Data Definition Language.

questions.text: Which SQL sub-language handles INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and SELECT?
questions.hint: It stands for Data Manipulation Language.

questions.text: Which SQL sub-language controls permissions (GRANT, REVOKE, DENY)?
questions.hint: It stands for Data Control Language.

questions.text: What is the default port number used by MySQL?
questions.hint: This is the standard MySQL port; remember it for troubleshooting connection issues.

questions.text: Which constraint uniquely identifies each row in a table?
questions.hint: It cannot contain NULL values and must be unique.

questions.text: Which constraint creates a link to the primary key of another table?
questions.hint: It maintains referential integrity between tables.

questions.text: Which constraint prevents a column from accepting NULL values?
questions.hint: The column must always have a value.

questions.text: Which statement correctly adds a new column to an existing table?
options: UPDATE TABLE users ADD Phone VARCHAR(20);
MODIFY TABLE users ADD Phone VARCHAR(20);
ALTER TABLE users ADD Phone VARCHAR(20);
INSERT INTO users ADD Phone VARCHAR(20);
questions.hint: ALTER TABLE is used for structural changes.

questions.text: What does AUTO_INCREMENT do when inserting a new row?
options: Sets the column value to zero
questions.hint: Commonly used with PRIMARY KEY columns.

questions.text: Which command permanently removes a table and all its data?
questions.hint: This is irreversible and removes both structure and data.

questions.text: Which command removes all rows from a table but keeps its structure?
questions.hint: Faster than DELETE and resets AUTO_INCREMENT.

questions.text: What happens if you run DELETE FROM users; without a WHERE clause?
options: Only the first row is deleted
The table structure is also dropped
questions.hint: Always use WHERE unless you intentionally want to empty the table.

questions.text: Which clause is used for pattern matching with wildcards?
questions.hint: LIKE is the correct operator for wildcards % and _.

questions.text: Which SQL clause sorts the results of a query?
questions.hint: You can specify ASC or DESC.

questions.text: Which command lets you start working inside a specific database?
questions.hint: Example: USE dbLending;

questions.text: Which constraint provides a fallback value when none is supplied during INSERT?
questions.hint: It automatically fills the column if omitted.

questions.text: What does the UNIQUE constraint do?
options: Makes the column the primary identifier
Prevents two rows from having the same value
questions.hint: Unlike PRIMARY KEY, it can allow one NULL in most databases.

questions.text: Which command gives a user permission to perform operations on a database object?
questions.hint: Example: GRANT SELECT, INSERT ON table TO 'user'@'localhost';

questions.text: Which command removes previously granted permissions?
questions.hint: It is the opposite of GRANT.

questions.text: What does DCL stand for?
questions.hint: It deals with user privileges and access control.

questions.text: Which PHP function is used to connect to MySQL using the mysqli extension?
questions.hint: It requires host, username, password, and database name.

questions.text: Which PHP function fetches a result row as an associative array?
questions.hint: You can access columns by name: $row['column_name']

questions.text: Which function returns the number of rows affected by an UPDATE, INSERT, or DELETE?
questions.hint: Useful for checking if a DML operation succeeded.

questions.text: What is the recommended way to prevent SQL injection in PHP?
questions.hint: PDO or mysqli prepared statements with bound parameters are safest.

questions.text: Which of the following is the more modern and secure database abstraction layer in PHP?
options: Both B and C are acceptable
questions.hint: PDO supports multiple databases; mysqli is MySQL-specific.

questions.text: Which JOIN returns only the rows that have matching values in both tables?
questions.hint: It is the most commonly used JOIN type.

questions.text: Which JOIN returns all rows from the left table and matching rows from the right table?
questions.hint: Non-matching right-side values appear as NULL.

questions.text: Which command-line tool is used to create a backup of a MySQL database?
questions.hint: Example: mysqldump -u root -p database_name > backup.sql

questions.text: How do you restore a database from a .sql backup file using the command line?
questions.hint: You redirect the file into the mysql client.

questions.text: If the WAMP icon is orange, what is the most common cause?
options: Port 80 or 443 is already in use
questions.hint: Skype or another web server often occupies port 80.

questions.text: What does the CHECK constraint do?
options: Ensures values meet a specific condition
questions.hint: Example: CHECK (Age >= 18)

questions.text: Which keyword is used to combine text from multiple columns into one?
questions.hint: Example: CONCAT(FirstName, ' ', LastName) AS FullName

questions.text: Which operator is used to select values within a range?
questions.hint: Syntax: WHERE Salary BETWEEN 40000 AND 60000

questions.text: What is the correct order of the four basic CRUD operations?
questions.hint: CRUD is a fundamental concept in database applications.

questions.text: Which of the following is a best practice for storing passwords?
options: Use password_hash() with a strong algorithm
Encrypt them with a fixed key
questions.hint: Never store plain-text passwords; use modern hashing.

questions.text: Which statement is true about the WHERE clause?
options: It is optional and never dangerous to omit
Omitting it on UPDATE or DELETE affects all rows
It can only be used with SELECT
questions.hint: Always double-check your WHERE conditions before running UPDATE/DELETE.

questions.text: Which tool provides a web-based graphical interface for managing MySQL databases in WAMP?
questions.hint: Accessible from the WAMP tray icon.

questions.text: Which SQL keyword is used to modify the structure of an existing table?
questions.hint: ALTER TABLE is the main command for structural changes.

questions.text: What does the DENY statement do?
options: Explicitly forbids a privilege even if granted
questions.hint: It overrides any GRANT statements.

questions.text: Which function checks how many rows a SELECT query returned?
questions.hint: Use this after a successful SELECT.

questions.text: Why is testing a backup important?
options: To ensure the backup can actually be restored
questions.hint: A backup that cannot be restored is useless.

questions.text: What should you use to prevent XSS (Cross-Site Scripting) when displaying user data?
questions.hint: It converts special characters to HTML entities.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly inserts data into specific columns only?
options: Both B and C are valid
questions.hint: You can omit columns that have defaults or are AUTO_INCREMENT.

questions.text: Which command shows all tables in the currently selected database?
questions.hint: Use after selecting a database with USE.

questions.text: Which command displays the structure of a table?
questions.hint: Also known as DESC table_name;

questions.text: In a self-referencing foreign key (e.g., ManagerID → EmpID), what kind of relationship is being modeled?
options: Hierarchical relationship within the same table
questions.hint: Common for employee-manager structures.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a recommended database design principle?
options: Use primary keys and foreign keys
Store passwords in plain text for easy recovery
questions.hint: Security best practices require hashing passwords.

questions.text: The local server stack acronym that turns a Windows PC into a mini internet (Windows + Apache + MySQL + PHP).
questions.hint: Green icon means everything is running.

questions.text: The SQL sub-language responsible for building and destroying table structures (CREATE, ALTER, DROP).
questions.hint: Stands for Data Definition Language.

questions.text: The SQL sub-language that handles INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, and SELECT.
questions.hint: Stands for Data Manipulation Language.

questions.text: The SQL sub-language that decides who gets the keys to the kingdom (permissions).
questions.hint: Stands for Data Control Language.

questions.text: The constraint that uniquely identifies every row in a table.
questions.hint: Cannot be NULL and must be unique.

questions.text: The constraint that points to another table's primary key and keeps relationships intact.
questions.hint: Enforces referential integrity.

questions.text: The constraint that simply refuses to accept emptiness in a column.
questions.hint: The column must always contain a value.

questions.text: The PHP function that connects your script to MySQL using the mysqli extension.
questions.hint: Also accept mysqli_connect().

questions.text: MySQL's default port number — memorize it, it'll show up when things break.
questions.hint: The standard TCP port for MySQL.

questions.text: The clause that saves you from accidentally nuking your entire table at 2am.
questions.hint: Always use it with UPDATE and DELETE.
